decisions.reason: As an extension of the established wafer business, it likely involved meaningful technical investment and remains close enough to the firm's core that management can justify continuing it despite limited visible market evidence.

This carrier wafer was publicly launched, fits the firm's stated push into handling and carrier solutions, and is the kind of adjacent product management is likely to retain because it supports the core portfolio and prior commitments.

The Cu-interposer glass wafer was introduced with a dedicated page and trade-fair launch, signaling visible commitment and development effort that make management inclined to persist unless failure is unmistakable.

Creating a separate brand for off-the-shelf wafers is a strong public commitment around a product line very close to the core business, so escalation of commitment makes withdrawal unlikely in the near term.

Glass-based circuit boards are more distant from the firm's narrow established offer, appear to have had less visible commitment than the other launches, and are therefore the product management is most likely to abandon to refocus resources.
